scope: Current framework backup and real installed GCS/Azure SDKs over local Postman HTTP simulations. No HTTP clients are mocked; no cloud account, VM or existing workspace is used.
implementation: Existing product adapters and snapshot/restore implementation pass unchanged. Added explicit opt-in acceptance, independent read-only HTTP contracts and execution context.

simulation.note: Totals include fixture-only observation GETs. Reported SDK case counts exclude those. Non-success responses are intentional failure cases; no 501 or mutating request occurred in the final run.
simulation.credentials: Anonymous GCS emulator credentials and a synthetic Azure SharedKey. No ADC, real account keys or cloud endpoints required.
simulation.owner_mock_search: Unavailable: Postman CLI unauthenticated. Repository-owned fixtures derive from vendor primary contracts linked in the operator contract.

verified: Both actual SDK paths capture two revisions, restore exact bytes and original document citation revision offline, preserve private file modes and retain source metadata.
Missing, denied, corrupt or oversized objects publish no snapshot; empty objects need no media read, and deliberately overlong responses are rejected.
Actual download requests carry bounded ranges. GCS download requests pin observed generation; 412 generation change and 503 service failure reject publication without retry.
Azure requests use real SDK SharedKey signing with synthetic credentials. This verifies request construction only, not cloud signature validation.
No object writes, deletes, bucket/object listing or provider requests during offline restore and reopened Studio. GCS SDK bucket metadata reads are separately modeled.
fixture_correction: Log inspection found optional GCS SDK bucket metadata reads initially returned 501. Final fixture serves documented Buckets.get; final SDK acceptance and logs contain no unsupported requests.
pending: Selected cloud-account authentication, IAM/permissions, retention/history and actual account restore drills.
Azure transient retry/backoff and slow/unreachable cloud-provider timing; only the stated failure shapes were tested.
Personal VM/account-store, physical device and installed-platform validation remain separate.
migration: No runtime, authentication, schema, API payload or stored configuration changes. New prerequisite-dependent acceptance is opt-in; normal required test discovery does not silently skip missing SDKs.
